funding: The AfricaMuseum is one of Belgium's ten federal scientific institutes and operates under the authority of the Secretary of State for Federal Science Policy, with the Belgian Federal Science Policy Office (BELSPO) commissioning its peer reviews. It employs some 190 people, including 50 scientists, and two thirds of its staff and budget go to scientific research. Director General Bart Ouvry heads the institution.
note: The museum had 106,000 visitors in 2024, down from 132,000 in 2023; it occupies the Charles Girault palace inaugurated by King Albert I in 1910.

propaganda.summary: King Leopold II created the museum in 1898 from the 1897 Brussels exposition's colonial section as a propaganda tool for his Congo colonial project; the 1910 building was opened to showcase the Belgian Congo.

n: Palais de la Porte Dorée (Musée national de l'histoire de l'immigration)
funding: The palace is run by the Établissement public du Palais de la Porte Dorée, an établissement public à caractère administratif placed under the joint supervision of four ministries, those responsible for integration, culture, national education and research. The body was formed in 2012 by merging the Cité nationale de l'histoire de l'immigration, itself created by decree in 2004 and made an établissement public in 2006, with the Aquarium de la Porte Dorée. Constance Rivière is its director general.
note: The permanent immigration exhibition opened in October 2007 and was fully reinstalled on 17 June 2023 after a three year closure; the 1931 Art Deco palace by Albert Laprade and Léon Jaussely covers 17,000 square metres.

propaganda.summary: Built 1928 to 1931 as the Musée des Colonies for the Paris Colonial Exhibition, the palace was a propaganda work made to promote the benefits of colonisation and the merits of the French empire.

funding: The museum is run by the foundation Stichting Nationaal Museum van Wereldculturen, operating since 2023 under the name Wereldmuseum, and has fallen under the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science since the 2014 merger that created the National Museum of World Cultures. Its collection is part of the Dutch national collection. The lottery VriendenLoterij is a supporting partner.
note: The museum had 317,572 visitors in 2022; it occupies the Colonial Institute building on Linnaeusstraat opened by Queen Wilhelmina in 1926, which it shared with the Royal Tropical Institute (KIT) until their separation in 2014.

propaganda.summary: The Colonial Institute's statutes charged its museum, opened 1926 with Ministry of Colonies funding, with promoting all interests stemming from the colonial possessions, an aim described as colonial propaganda; renamed in 1950.

funding: The monument is managed by EGEAC (Empresa de Gestão de Equipamentos e Animação Cultural), the municipal company of the Câmara Municipal de Lisboa that runs the city's cultural venues, which took over its management in April 2003. EGEAC's 2025 plan and budget lists the Padrão among its venues with a forecast of 221,664 visitors. The Portuguese Republic holds title to the monument.
note: The 56 metre concrete and stone slab on the Belém waterfront was remodelled in 1985 with an auditorium, exhibition halls and a rooftop viewpoint; EGEAC's 2025 programme centres on expansion, empire and colonial memories.

propaganda.summary: The Estado Novo rebuilt the 1940 Portuguese World Exhibition monument in concrete in 1960 for the Henry the Navigator quincentenary; scholars call it the regime's brand image and a monument of its ideology.

funding: The monument has been run as a Section 21 (non-profit) company since 1993, with the affiliated Heritage Foundation (Erfenisstigting) established in 2002. In 2011 it told Parliament that tourism supplied 56 to 60 percent of its revenue and that the Department of Arts and Culture grant, R1,853,000 in 2010, was a small share of an operating budget that had grown to R14 million a year. It was declared a National Heritage Site by SAHRA on 8 July 2011.
note: The granite monument by Gerard Moerdijk stands in a nature reserve with an amphitheatre for 20,000 people built in 1949; Major General (retired) Gert Opperman led it as CEO from 2000.

propaganda.summary: Inaugurated 16 December 1949 by Prime Minister Malan with mostly government funding, the monument gave the new National Party government a stage to celebrate the volk and articulate white supremacy.

funding: The National Palace Museum is a state-funded agency placed directly under the Executive Yuan, the cabinet of the Republic of China, alongside the Central Bank and two directorates-general. Its budget is voted by the Legislative Yuan, which froze a NT$350 million renovation budget in December 2024 and over 20 percent of its budget in 2025. Director Hsiao Tsung-huang has led it since January 2023.
note: Visits fell from a record 6.14 million in 2016 to 2.87 million in 2024 across the Taipei and Chiayi branches; the Waishuangxi building opened on 12 November 1965.

propaganda.summary: Opened by the KMT government in 1965, the museum served to assert the KMT's legitimacy as the sole legitimate Chinese government and to educate Taiwanese about their Chinese heritage.

funding: Responsibility for all services at Anıtkabir belongs to the General Staff of the Turkish Armed Forces, which took control after the 1980 coup, and the site is run as a military installation open free to the public. Visitor figures are published by the Anıtkabir Command and shared by the Ministry of National Defence. A 1981 law declared the site a national monument.
note: Anıtkabir received 6,550,480 visitors in 2024 and 1,092,000 on 10 November 2024 alone; the mausoleum, built from 1944, opened in 1953 and its Atatürk and War of Independence Museum opened in 1960.

propaganda.summary: Run by the Turkish General Staff since 1980, Anıtkabir presents an authorized version of Turkish history; official visits and ceremonies honour Atatürk and the Republic, re-sacralising the Atatürk cult.
